statement.p:
(a) Supposed that at (3,3), we know that f_x=f_y=0 and f_{xx} = 0, f_{yy} = 0, and f_{xy} > 0. What can we conclude about the behavior of this function near the point (3,3)?
?
(3,3) is a local maximum
(3,3) is a local minimum
(3,3) is a saddle point
(3,3) is a none of these

(b) Supposed that at (5,5), we know that f_x=f_y=0 and f_{xx} = 0, f_{yy} > 0, and f_{xy} \lt 0. What can we conclude about the behavior of this function near the point (5,5)?
?
(5,5) is a local maximum
(5,5) is a local minimum
(5,5) is a saddle point
(5,5) is a none of these

(c) Supposed that at (7,6), we know that f_x=f_y=0 and f_{xx} = 0, f_{yy} \lt 0, and f_{xy} > 0. What can we conclude about the behavior of this function near the point (7,6)?
?
(7,6) is a local maximum
(7,6) is a local minimum
(7,6) is a saddle point
(7,6) is a none of these
Using this information, on a separate sheet of paper sketch a possible contour diagram for f.

static.solution:
f_x = f_y = 0, so each of the three points is a critical point. Then we have D = f_{xx} f_{yy} - (f_{xy})^2, so we know that
(a) At (3,3), D \lt 0, so (3,3) is a saddle point.
(b) At (5,5), D \lt 0, so (5,5) is a saddle point.
(c) At (7,6), D \lt 0, so (7,6) is a saddle point.
